findings.summary: Gate/status projection is source-sensitive and historical candidate fixes were not freshly compiled or accepted.
Reason precedence and secondary reasons require acceptance beyond the source candidate.
Namespaced gate-kind matching remains a contract concern; no fresh Rust proof.
Guidance/status source uses durable context paths, but authenticated identity/session authorization is incomplete.
Canonical unix-ms parsing exists in source, but compatibility and timer behavior are not accepted.
Malformed prerequisite/corruption propagation remains a source and validation gap.
Hold resolution route exists, but exact principal/project/replay and force/waiver boundaries are not accepted.
The retained source-archive .cjs omission was repaired in the historical candidate, but packaging/release acceptance remains separate.
The specific fixture-version mismatch was reconciled; independent contract acceptance is still absent.
Profiles/gates and closeout records exist, but authoritative independent profile declarations remain unresolved.
Finish/close/release/reopen transaction-wide canonical re-evaluation is not established.
Expiry history/disposition before reclaim remains an unresolved lifecycle boundary.
Current v2 registry is not a complete v1 runtime/command inventory or import provenance.
Not-before/due/overdue scheduling and complete safe-next semantics remain incomplete.
Container status is represented, but exact descendant rollups/readiness are not accepted.
Independent review decisions and gate-force/dependency-waiver public routes are unavailable.
Malformed-row tolerance, transitive corruption diagnostics and pagination/count reconciliation remain unresolved.
Canonical claim snapshot/write transaction performance has no current queue-wait versus hold-time evidence.
Canonical clocks and registered actors are required by current paths; compatibility/import signoff is open.
Operation readback/recovery structures exist, but rejected and unknown outcomes are not real-service proven.
The historical candidate had no Rust execution/reviewer/service proof; current tools are recorded available but this task did not run them.
Planning/cycle/sprint/workflow/queue parity, migration, isolation, and release gates remain incomplete.
Internal cycle/intake groundwork and handlers coexist with public registry gaps; source/spec capability drift must be resolved before exposing routes.
Source routes are direct-only while protocol/service route parity and source-to-memory publication are absent.
Recovery/doctor and runtime recovery types exist, but operator recovery, durable operation outcomes, and restart/readback are not validated end to end.
TUI exposes mounted lifecycle actions and service-shaped calls, but fixture/controller tests do not prove real service route parity or complete planning/review/recovery UX.
Update/upgrade source implementations exist, but installer identity, atomic upgrade/rollback, supported platforms, schema-safe rollback, and publication are not production-proven.
